Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we have alignment before I loop in Solutions/Finance:

- Estimated monthly token range from your pilot signals: 50M — 180M tokens (conservative) with a mid scenario ~110M.
- Unit economics target you flagged: goal of ~$850 / 1M tokens (this is your procurement target range).
- Based on Redwood pricing profiles, the approximate monthly spend band for that token range is: $47k — $153k (depending on model mix and KV cache hit rate).
- Procurement path: Tom indicated PO process for anything > $75k needs Procurement + VP sign-off; anything < $75k can be handled by engineering/finance team approvals.

Attachments: I attached an updated pilot quote (rdw-pilot-quote-v2.pdf) with the three model variants we discussed + an example procurement checklist (procurement-checklist-fintegrate.xlsx).

Action items / next steps:
1) Sara: confirm whether Procurement considers $75k the hard threshold for VP review, or if there are speed lanes for pilot PO routing.
2) Tom: if the $75k threshold is correct, can you share the likely sign-off timeline (1 week / 2 weeks)?
3) Monica: I asked Product to prepare a short ops note on prefix caching assumptions for the pilot — will share Tuesday.
4) Karthik (me): I’ll prepare a one-page cost sensitivity table showing spend vs cache hit and model mix (attached in the quote).

If that looks right I’ll schedule a short call with Procurement and Legal to confirm lead times and any DocuSign/contract redlines. Suggested times: Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Karthik

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick answers below:

- Confirming the token estimates — 50M conservative, 110M likely, 180M high. We’ll aim to size the pilot at 110M/month.
- Procurement threshold: correct, $75k is the internal threshold that forces VP-level sign-off. Anything under $75k flows through Procurement and can be executed in ~5 business days. Above $75k typically takes 10–15 business days due to committee review.
- Legal: we use an outside counsel review only for contracts that modify liability/terms (rarely for pilots). If Redwood’s standard SOW + MSA is used, our Legal will usually sign off in 3–5 business days after Procurement clears it.

I’ll ping Procurement and ask Tom to schedule a quick sync if you want Procurement on the call.

Folks —

Quick procurement notes from my side so we can set expectations for lead times:

- If we keep the pilot cap <= $75k/month we’ll route through our normal Procurement lane; typical turnaround is 3–7 business days for a PO after we get a final SOW and quote.
- If the pilot hits a spend that suggests multi-month commitments (>$225k total contract value) Procurement will want an exec-level sponsorship and formal Finance review.
- For pilots that might scale quickly, we sometimes do a two-stage PO: an initial PO for the first month (smaller amount) and a follow-up rolling PO to cover scale — that can reduce legal lead time.

Lauren / Monica — could you confirm whether Redwood can support a two-stage PO approach and a 30-day invoice term for pilots? If so, I can prepare the internal PO template and route.

Tom
Procurement Manager, Fintegrate
